title: ftypes + dfilter: Convert booleans from strings in semcheck
description:
Don't have a boolean_from_string function in ftypes, because it
causes the strings "True" and "False" to match with FT_BOOLEANs that
have different value strings - even though like `flexray.nfi` that
map "True" and "False" to reversed values. (ed.: This is confusing
and probably some other true_false_string should be used instead.)

Instead, similar to before 4b6268c01eb8e8f4e96760a89552ca9672069c3f
use the default true_false_string inside semcheck in
mk_fvalue_from_val_string if the FT_BOOLEAN does not have its
own true_false_string. One problem identified by that commit has
been fixed in later commmits - a FT_BOOLEAN fvalue is created
instead of a FT_UINT64.

Other changes have created greater separation between unquoted literals
and quoted strings, which helps make this unambiguous. An unquoted
literal for a FT_BOOLEAN true and false matches (case-insensitively)
1 and 0, respectively. This holds for all FT_BOOLEANs, regardless of
their true_false_string. Quoted strings *only* match the FT_BOOLEAN
true_false_string, with the default string used for any FT_BOOLEAN
that does not have its own true_false_string.

There's an argument for allowing with a deprecation warning quoted
"True" or "False" for FT_BOOLEANs that have their own true_false_string,
although that creates some possible confusion with fields like
`flexray.nfi`.

Fix #20262
